cues.text: Jerry, how did it go with preparing your lessons? Is there anything you would like to discuss?
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: Well, this is actually the first time that I have ever taught in an elementary classroom.
cues.speaker: Jerry

cues.text: After 8 years of learning pedagogy, I want to practice what I’ve learned in an instructive manner, but I’m a bit stuck right now.
cues.speaker: Jerry

cues.text: You know the topic 1 want them to research is a bit hard for pupils.
cues.speaker: Jerry

cues.text: I’m afraid that they won’t be able to handle it on their own.
cues.speaker: Jerry

cues.text: So I need new ideas on designing more effective teaching methods.
cues.speaker: Jerry

cues.text: Mr.Carter, do you have any suggestions?
cues.speaker: Jerry

cues.text: Well, you should probably read this book called Professional Learning, written by J.K. Simmons.
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: He is a professor who just transferred here last semester but is already popular amongst the students for his creative teaching methods.
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: There is an extensive range of learning approaches mentioned in the book including approaches for team research, which might be helpful to you.
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: You mean dividing the students into groups to do research?
cues.speaker: Jerry

cues.text: I’ve never thought of this before. How does it work?
cues.speaker: Jerry

cues.text: Professor Simmons has already demonstrated how efficient this approach can be.
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: Basically it aims to increase cooperation between students so they can present the results in a collaborative fashion.
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: It helps them to develop their own voice and perspective.
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: I’ll check out the book as soon as possible.
cues.speaker: Jerry

cues.text: It seems I can borrow some of the essential concepts and work them into my course design.
cues.speaker: Jerry

cues.text: Well, I was thinking maybe I could use both observation and nonobservation as part of my teaching methodology.
cues.speaker: Jerry

cues.text: Could you take a look at my teaching plan?
cues.speaker: Jerry

cues.text: Sure. What kind of observational methods do you have in mind?
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: For the observational part, I intend to include two approaches.
cues.speaker: Jerry

cues.text: First, the pupils can assess each other’s behaviour.
cues.speaker: Jerry

cues.text: I feel that reviewing fellow students through criteria-based reference evaluation allows constructive feedback.
cues.speaker: Jerry

cues.text: It can also improve their understanding of the subject material.
cues.speaker: Jerry

cues.text: That’s a smart move for a large class that would be hard to observe all by yourself.
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: Also, you might want to get the feedback from several different individuals rather than just one.
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: So how do you plan to carry out the peer assessments?
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: Oh, every pupil will be required to write a diary, which includes group projects, presentations and in-class discussions.
cues.speaker: Jerry

cues.text: They’ll put down their remarks. I’ll collect them on a regular basis which can also help me see whether they can keep up or not.
cues.speaker: Jerry

cues.text: Good, what else do you intend to do?
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: Besides that, I also plan to do video recording.
cues.speaker: Jerry

cues.text: I’ve already purchased a camera just in case I miss anything important.
cues.speaker: Jerry

cues.text: I can go back and review their performances anytime I want.
cues.speaker: Jerry

cues.text: Would you record every in-class activity?
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: No, I’ll just keep track of an in-class simulation, which would require every pupil to fully participate.
cues.speaker: Jerry

cues.text: Students will act as members of a City Council meeting, discussing issues like whether or not prohibition should be instated in the United States.
cues.speaker: Jerry

cues.text: This kind of teaching method is both inspiring and challenging.
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: I can’t wait to see how yours work out. Do you send me a copy of the assessment afterwards, will you?
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: No problem.
cues.speaker: Jerry

cues.text: So what do you have in mind for the non-observational approaches?
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: Well, my plan is to quantify the statistics. Numbers do not lie.
cues.speaker: Jerry

cues.text: It is the most direct way to measure their performance. See how well they’ve learned.
cues.speaker: Jerry

cues.text: Where does the data come from?
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: I’ll evaluate the test results including the mid-term, final exam and pop quizzes, which would only take up about 40 percent of the overall assessment.
cues.speaker: Jerry

cues.text: Sounds like a lot of tests and assignments. Please remember that you don’t want to wear out your students.
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: Keeping them engaged is the key to efficient learning. Once they are exhausted, they just stop trying.
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: Oh, I haven’t thought about that. You are right.
cues.speaker: Jerry

cues.text: I don’t want to frighten them with tons of assignments and exams. I’ll make note of that. Thanks for the advice.
cues.speaker: Jerry

cues.text: I remember last time you mentioned questionnaires, right?
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: That’s true. But it is not for my students.
cues.speaker: Jerry

cues.text: In fact, they have to design their own questionnaires and choose the respondents using the Internet.
cues.speaker: Jerry

cues.text: As a complement of other teaching activities, it would deepen the creative learning process.
cues.speaker: Jerry

cues.text: Is that all?
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: Oh, the pupils will have to conduct interviews of their own.
cues.speaker: Jerry

cues.text: And for this, they get to choose anyone they like, including relatives, friends and acquaintances to answer the questions.
cues.speaker: Jerry

cues.text: Seems to me that you have figured out most of your teaching methods. But you still need to polish some of the activities...
cues.speaker: Tutor
